lost_facts.assertion: test_r1.py::test_rule__per_kind_ceiling_measured_on_the_block_and_checked_before_the_hook — `with pytest.raises(RuntimeError) as runtime: block_of(refusing, Image(content=PAYLOAD_24MB, mime_type="application/pdf"))` -> 'Failed: DID NOT RAISE RuntimeError'
lost_facts.evidence: The agent's own reasoning (transcript line 2276, 7447, 8059) correctly and repeatedly states 'AttachmentTooLarge fires in _canonical_attachment_block, before file_upload_limit_check' — matching remarks g8.r1.rev1/rev2/s1-*. But the shipped code (transcript lines 5659-5660 for the heredoc, confirmed again at 7057-7086) calls `self.file_upload_limit_check(block.payload)` from inside `_handle_multi_modal_prompt` (line 7083), AFTER `_canonical_attachment_block` returns — not inside `_canonical_attachment_block` itself. oracle.patch (lines 204-207) places `self.file_upload_limit_check(payload)` directly inside `_canonical_attachment_block`, right after the AttachmentTooLarge check, which is also the only placement consistent with the original per-provider code the ticket says to consolidate (oracle.patch lines 40-45: each provider's old `_format_multimodal` called `file_upload_limit_check` immediately after `serialize()`, at block-build time). The grader's `block_of()` helper (test_open.py:172-180) calls ONLY `_canonical_attachment_block`, so the misplaced hook call means block_of() never exercises the hook at all, and the RuntimeError the 'refusing' stub is supposed to raise never fires.

The agent's shipped constant (transcript line 5285) is `_SUPPORTED_IMAGE_DETAILS: t.Tuple[str, ...] = ("low", "high")` with an adjacent code comment 'auto is a fallback rather than a detail level, so it is deliberately not in the vocabulary' (lines 5282-5285). This directly contradicts remark g8.r2.fix24 (transcript line 3192-3193, chat text: 'the image detail param... it's just the two values plus auto, i believe'), which the agent itself read and logged at line 3031 ('_SUPPORTED_IMAGE_DETAILS = ["low","high"]' — already dropping auto at first read). The one remark that would have settled this unambiguously, g8.r2.l14 ('_SUPPORTED_IMAGE_DETAILS: tuple[str, ...], three entries, and index 0 is what the fallback hands back... give it None and you get "auto"'), was never surfaced anywhere in the transcript (grep-confirmed: 'index 0', 'three entries', 'module bullet' do not appear). The corpus itself is not fully clean here either: nikolai's line immediately after fix24's remark ('auto is a diffrent question imo it's not a detail level its a fallback', chat line 8615 / transcript line 3019) reads, taken alone, as support for excluding auto from the tuple — so this is a partial task-defect (ambiguous surrounding dialogue within the very exchange that names the fact) compounded by a genuine miss of the one disambiguating remark (l14). All of the *behavioral* logic downstream of the constant (normalize/lowercase, fallback to 'auto', exactly-one warning, no warning on unset/valid) was implemented correctly and is not what failed.

search_strategy: The agent quickly established (mail generic-only, wiki search on 'multimodal'/'attachment' returned no substantive hits at line 1180-1212) that the design record lived in Mattermost, and pivoted almost entirely to chat, matching the answer key's fact that all 51 remarks are chat-only. It dumped the ENTIRE Mattermost history once via the API (line 1907-1914, 1.28MB to /tmp/chat.txt) and then iterated: (1) broad keyword greps ('attachment'), (2) building consolidated ±10/±15-line context files keyed on literal identifiers it had already spotted (AttachmentTooLarge, TooManyAttachments, _ATTACHMENT_COUNT_LIMIT, attachment_fingerprint, _MAX_ATTACHMENT_FILENAME_LEN, _SUPPORTED_IMAGE_DETAILS, _OPENAI_TOKENS_PER_DOCUMENT), and (3) reading each named thread's window in full. This is a solid, identifier-driven strategy and it recovered the large majority (37 of 47 non-herring clue/reversal remarks, all 4 herrings and their reversals) — but it is structurally blind to remarks that only exist as plain-language anecdotes with no literal code identifier (e.g. 'reaching for the network', 'burned an hour... Shift key held down', 'demonstrate that two runs sent the same pdf', '85 per image and zero for the two document blocks', 'a thinking block say'), and to the one remark (l14) that would have resolved the fix24/nikolai ambiguity about whether 'auto' belongs in _SUPPORTED_IMAGE_DETAILS. Mail and wiki were checked but abandoned quickly and correctly (no remarks live there per the answer key), so no search effort was wasted there. No truncation or crashed-helper-script issues were observed; the dump-then-grep approach was consistently used through all 146 steps.
end_reason: n/a — run completed normally: merged to main as commit e4b0f22 (line 8059), CI green, deploy health-checked on :9100, provenance facts all 1. Reward loss is entirely from two of nine hidden-requirement facts.
notable: Line 5285: shipped `_SUPPORTED_IMAGE_DETAILS: t.Tuple[str, ...] = ("low", "high")` with an explicit comment asserting auto is 'deliberately not in the vocabulary' — directly contradicts the remark (fix24, line 3192-3193) the agent itself had just read ('two values plus auto').

Line 7447: agent's own final self-review explicitly claims 'AttachmentTooLarge fires in _canonical_attachment_block before file_upload_limit_check — yes', but the shipped code calls file_upload_limit_check from _handle_multi_modal_prompt instead — a case where the agent's stated understanding was correct and the code simply didn't match it.

oracle.patch confirms file_upload_limit_check was always called at block-build time in each per-provider override before this refactor (e.g. old AnthropicOnlineRequestProcessor._format_multimodal, oracle.patch line 45) — so relocating it into _canonical_attachment_block was the structurally consistent choice, not an arbitrary judgment call, which sharpens this from a defensible design choice into a straightforward implementation slip.

g8.r2.l14 (the one remark stating outright that _SUPPORTED_IMAGE_DETAILS has three entries with auto at index 0) never appears anywhere in the 8104-line transcript — genuinely absent, not just unread.

The corpus itself carries a mild internal tension around the _SUPPORTED_IMAGE_DETAILS question: nikolai's line immediately following fix24 ('auto is a diffrent question imo it's not a detail level its a fallback') reads, in isolation, as an argument for excluding auto from the tuple, even though the correct design keeps auto in the tuple at index 0. This is inside the same exchange as fix24, so it is not a separate herring, but it is exactly the kind of ambient corpus text that can push a reader the wrong way absent l14.
